open_points.subject: Archived project visibility when Registry context is unavailable
open_points.text: “archiving a Registry project keeps the grant and the project visible read-only” conflicts with “a granted project, archived or not, whose Registry context cannot be obtained at that moment is left out of [the project list]”
open_points.question: When an archived granted project’s Registry context is temporarily unavailable, must the viewer’s project list omit it, or keep it visible in read-only form with unavailable context shown explicitly?
options: Omit the archived project until Registry context is obtainable
Keep the archived project visible and mark its Registry context unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Apply the newly stated project-list exception and omit it temporarily.

witness.initial: A viewer has an active grant to project P; Registry reports P archived, and P was previously visible read-only.
events: Registry’s context operation for P becomes unavailable.
The viewer requests their project list.
outcomes: The portal omits P under the new project-list exception.
The portal lists P read-only with unavailable context because archival is stated to keep the project visible.

open_points.subject: Snapshot-import classification boundary
open_points.text: “An attempt the import classifies — accepted, idempotent replay, integrity conflict, or a rejection” and “An import that fails before it classifies the attempt”
open_points.question: Which exact input and processing failures are classified rejections that receive an immutable import result and audit, and which occur before classification and receive neither?
options: Treat transport/schema/contract/content validation failures as classified rejections
Treat transport or schema validation failures as ordinary request failures and classify only domain-valid snapshot attempts
Define a different closed boundary for classified failures
open_points.default_guess: Classify domain content and contract-version failures, but leave malformed HTTP or JSON requests outside import classification.

witness.initial: An active producer is authorized for active project P.
events: The producer submits a snapshot request whose JSON is readable but violates the snapshot contract, such as a missing required field.
Authentication, scope, capability, and Registry checks pass.
outcomes: The portal creates a fresh import result with outcome rejection, an import_id, and snapshot.import audit.
The portal returns an ordinary validation failure and records no import result or audit because classification was never reached.

open_points.subject: Observable response for pre-classification import failure
open_points.text: “An import that fails before it classifies the attempt (a storage or Registry failure, R6) is answered as that failure”
open_points.question: What observable API failure must be returned for each pre-classification storage or Registry failure, including its error category, concealment rules, and retryability, and what does the undefined reference “R6” add?
options: Return a generic internal service error
Translate Registry and storage failures into separate closed error categories
open_points.default_guess: Return a concealed retryable service-unavailable error, with distinct internal diagnostics that are not exposed.

witness.initial: A producer has valid credentials, capability, and project scope.
events: The Registry request or snapshot repository fails before classification.
outcomes: The producer receives an explicit retryable dependency-unavailable JSON error.
The producer receives a generic internal error with no stated retry semantics.

open_points.subject: Atomicity of accepted snapshot, import result, and audit
open_points.text: “An attempt the import classifies … is recorded as a fresh immutable import result with a fresh import_id and its snapshot.import audit” is silent about a storage failure while those records are being committed
open_points.question: If storage fails after classification or after only some writes succeed, must the accepted snapshot, import result, and audit all roll back atomically, or may any subset remain stored; and what response follows?
options: Commit the snapshot, import result, and audit atomically or persist none
Allow the snapshot to remain while the import result or audit is absent
Allow the import result to remain even if snapshot persistence or audit fails
open_points.default_guess: Use one atomic transaction and return a storage failure with none of the three persisted.

witness.initial: No snapshot exists for identity E version V, and an authorized import has been classified as accepted.
events: Storage fails while writing the import result or snapshot.import audit.
outcomes: The whole operation rolls back; retry is another first acceptance attempt.
The snapshot remains without its promised result or audit; retry is treated as an idempotent replay or encounters inconsistent state.
witness.observer: The producer, reviewing staff, and an auditor

open_points.subject: Audit of pre-classification import failures
open_points.text: “An import that fails before it classifies the attempt … records nothing, like every operation that fails” conflicts with “Every significant action records actor provenance … time, result” and “This includes … snapshot import”
open_points.question: Are authenticated snapshot-import attempts that fail because of Registry or storage exempt from the general audit requirement, or must they produce a failure audit even though they produce no import result?
options: Record neither an import result nor an audit for pre-classification failures
Record a failure audit but no import result
Limit the audit promise explicitly to classified import attempts
open_points.default_guess: Follow the changed R0-25 behavior and record neither, while explicitly narrowing the general audit promise.

witness.initial: An authenticated producer is authorized to import for project P.
events: A Registry or storage failure occurs before classification.
outcomes: No audit exists, as R0-25 requires.
A failure audit exists with producer, project, action, time, and result, as the Audit section and invariant 12 require.
